description: Understand hosts, ports, services and observations in a private, authorized practice environment. Guided explanations, six original visual diagrams, safe practice, trusted resource links, worked examples and a randomized quiz.

blocks.text: Lesson 4 — Network discovery inside your own lab

LEARNING OUTCOME
Understand hosts, ports, services and observations in a private, authorized practice environment.

Safety rule: work only with devices, accounts and training applications you own or have explicit written permission to assess. Use synthetic information. A public system or a suspicious person is not permission.

A host is a device or virtual system; a port is a logical service endpoint; a service is the application listening there. A discovery result is an observation, not proof of a weakness. Compare observations with the documented design and authorized scope.

blocks.text: Use the exact private target supplied in your course lab, not an arbitrary public address. Begin with the lab checklist and tool documentation. Keep intensity within the rules of engagement and save only the output needed for the report.

blocks.text: Record target ID, service, expected and observed behavior, timestamp, evidence reference, impact, confidence and follow-up. If a host is outside scope, do not test it further.

blocks.text: Practice checklist: (1) read the lab rules, (2) use fabricated data or an isolated training target, (3) predict what the control should do, (4) test one small condition, (5) save only minimal evidence, and (6) explain the defensive follow-up. Stop and ask the owner if any target or action is outside the approved scope.

blocks.output: Use the supplied lab target. Do not substitute an unrelated public address.

blocks.question: Before Lesson 4 testing, what should be confirmed?
options: A friend said it is okay
The exact target is covered by written permission

blocks.question: How should a finding from Lesson 4 be handled?
options: Save minimal redacted evidence and report through the approved channel
Include a real password as proof
